title: The matter-antimatter asymmetry: which baryogenesis mechanism
bottleneck: The observable universe contains essentially no primordial antimatter, yet the Standard Model's CP violation and out-of-equilibrium processes fall far short of generating the observed baryon-to-photon ratio of six parts in ten billion. Sakharov's conditions are understood, but no specific mechanism is confirmed.
why_it_blocks: Our very existence as matter rather than radiation is unexplained; solving baryogenesis is required for any complete account of the early universe.
current_state: Electroweak baryogenesis is squeezed by Higgs and electric-dipole-moment constraints, leptogenesis is elegant but untestable at its natural scale, and Affleck-Dine and other scenarios await any experimental handle. Sakharov's conditions are necessary but not sufficient; the Standard Model's CP violation falls short of the observed asymmetry by many orders of magnitude, so new sources of CP violation or out-of-equilibrium dynamics are mandatory.
